title: sfnx04
Who is Imam Ali?
hook: He was born inside the Kaaba. He lay down in the Prophet's bed. He is the gate of the city of knowledge.
scenes.0.text: Thirty years after the year of the elephant, on the thirteenth day of the month of Recep, Fatimah bint Ased's labor began in Mecca. She went to the Ka'bah, spread her hands and prayed to Allah to ease her delivery. Then the wall of the House was rent. Fatima bint Ased came in and closed herself behind the wall. Those outside tried to open the door, but they couldn't. **Ali** was born in the house of Allah. He stayed there with his mother for three days. On the fourth day, Fatima bint Ased left the Kaaba with her baby in her arms. No one before or since was born in the Kaaba.

scenes.1.text: When **Ali** was a young boy, there was a famine in Mecca. His father, Abu Talib, had a large family, and living was becoming increasingly difficult. The Prophet wanted to lighten the burden of his uncle, who raised him as a child, and took the young Ali into his home. Ali grew up in the house of the Prophet before the revelation came. He saw her not only in the crowd, but at the table, on the street and in the silence of the night. He watched her speech, her compassion and her honesty as a son would his father. These years spent with the Prophet shaped Ali's entire life.

scenes.2.text: When the first revelation came to the Prophet, **Ali** was a young man. The invitation to Islam began with a few people in a small house in those days. Ali was one of the first people to believe in the word of the Prophet. Sources give different rankings as to who first embraced Islam. Some refer to Hadeeth, some to Abu Bakr. The Shia reading says that the first man to believe was Ali. His young age did not diminish the value of his faith. While all the elders of Mecca turned their backs on the Prophet, this young man who grew up in his house believed him without hesitation and stood by him.

scenes.3.text: On the night of the migration, the idolaters of Mecca conspired to kill the Prophet. At night, the house was surrounded by armed men. The plan was to attack all together when the Prophet left his house in the morning. The Prophet was about to leave for Medina that night. Someone had to sleep in his bed instead so that people outside would think he was home. **Ali** accepted the assignment without thinking. She lay down on the Prophet's bed and covered herself with his mantle. The prophet left the house in the darkness of the night. The men at the door waited until morning. This night is called Laylatul-Ma'bît, the night of sleeping in bed.

scenes.4.text: When morning came, the pagans drawn their swords and stormed into the house. When they lifted the covering of the bed, they found **Ali**, not the Prophet. And they turned back in confusion, while he had gone away. Surah Bakara, verse 207, speaks of one who gives up his life to seek the pleasure of Allah: "And among the people is he who sells his life to seek the pleasure of Allah". Shia and some Sunni commentaries say that this verse was revealed on Ali that night. Other sources associate the verse with other Sahaba. But when the Prophet is in bed, waiting for the morning at the risk of his death, the sources converge.

scenes.5.text: After the migration, Medina became a new home for Muslims. The emigrants from Mecca left their homes and possessions behind. The Prophet declared them brothers of the Ansar, the natives of Medina. He gave each Muhajir an Ansar brother. When it came to **Ali**, the Prophet did not match him to anyone. He turned to him and said, "You are my brother in this world and in the Hereafter". So he chose Ali as his brother, not someone else's. This word showed the place of Ali in the heart of the Prophet to everyone in Medina.

scenes.6.text: During the years of Medina, **Ali** fought alongside the Prophet at Badr, Uhud and Hendek. The Muslim flag was often in his hand. When the siege of Khaybar was prolonged for several days, the Prophet said, "I will give the flag of tomorrow to someone who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him". That night, each of the companions slept expecting to be given the flag. In the morning, the Prophet summoned Ali. Ali's eyes hurt, but when he came to the Prophet, his eyes healed and the banner was given to him. Khyber was conquered that day by the hand of Ali.

scenes.7.text: One of the sayings of the Prophet to **Ali** is: "I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate". This hadith is accepted by many Sunni rabbis as valid, while Shiites accept it as obligatory. The metaphor is obvious. Whoever enters a city, enters through the gate. Anyone who tries to jump over the walls won't make it to the city. And whoever wishes to attain the knowledge that the Prophet brought, he should seek it from Ali. Imams who came after him passed this knowledge from father to son. The Shi'ites, when they learn their religion, enter through the door of the Ehl-i Beyt on this basis.

scenes.8.text: Allah commands the Prophet to say, "I do not ask you for any reward for this except love for my relatives". This verse shows that love of neighbor is the only way to repay a prophet's commission. In the commentary, which focuses on the Ehl-i Beyt, these relatives are Hz **Ali**, Hz **Fatima**, Hz **Hasan** and Hz Husayn. Some Sunni scholars interpret the verse as a kinship with Quraysh. In Shia reading, this love is not just an emotion. It means acknowledging their rights, listening to their words, and following their ways. The Prophet asked his people to love this family as a reward for all their hard work.

scenes.11.text: When the Prophet passed away, **Ali** was at his head. He closed his blessed eyes. According to Ahl al-Bayt, the Prophet (peace be upon him) had willed that Ali (peace be upon him) wash him. Ali began to wash the Prophet's body in tears. Around the same time, in a corner of Medina, in Sakife, they were discussing who would take over after the Prophet. Ali, who raised his hand in Ghadir, was not invited to that meeting. At that time he was in charge of the most precious trust, the blessed body of the Prophet.

sunni.0.says: Al-Hakim corrects Mus'ab al-Zubayri's statement "No one was born in the Kaaba before him or after him" and says: "The reports are mutawatir: Fatima bint Asad gave birth to the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali b. Abi Talib inside the Kaaba." Ibn al-Mulaqqin, in al-Badr al-Munir, vol. 6, p. 489, records that this sentence appears in al-Mustadrak in the biography of Imam Ali.
sunni.0.grade: Al-Hakim's own judgment; here, tawatur is his wording
sunni.1.says: While narrating the caliphate of Imam Ali b. Abi Talib, it is said, "His birth was in the Kaaba."
sunni.2.says: Reports about Imam Ali's early conversion to Islam; there is disagreement over the order of the first Muslims.
sunni.3.says: The Prophet's saying to Imam Ali, "You are my brother in this world and the hereafter."
sunni.4.says: The Prophet's saying at Khaybar that he would give the banner to one who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by them; the man turns out to be Imam Ali.
sunni.5.says: "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate."
sunni.5.grade: Its authenticity is disputed: Tirmidhi/al-Hakim transmitted it; some hadith scholars consider it weak or fabricated. Ibn Hajar's view that it should not be declared weak was conveyed through WikiShia.
sunni.6.says: A report concerning the Prophet's sword called Dhu al-Fiqar; the saying "la fata illa Ali" is not part of this report.
sunni.6.grade: The saying "La fata illa Ali" is generally considered weak/disputed
sunni.7.says: The interpretation that the term "near kin" points to kinship with the Quraysh.
sunni.8.says: The report that Imam Ali took part in washing the Prophet.
sunni.9.says: Imam Ali's lying in the Prophet's bed on the night of the Hijra.
shia.0.says: Imam Ali was born on Friday, 13 Rajab, thirty years after the Year of the Elephant, in Mecca, in the Bayt Allah. No one was born in God's house before him or after him; this is God's honor to him. His mother is Fatima bint Asad.
shia.1.says: From Yazid b. Ka'nab: When Fatima bint Asad went into labor, she prayed beside the Kaaba. The back of the house opened, she went in, and the wall closed.
shia.2.says: Yazid b. Ka'nab: The back of the Kaaba opened and Fatima bint Asad entered. On the fourth day she came out with Imam Ali in her arms. The footnote on the page links the same report with Ilal al-Shara'i' 135/3.
shia.3.says: Laylat al-Mabit and Imam Ali's lying in the Prophet's bed.
shia.4.says: The event of the night of the Hijra and the report on Baqara 207.
shia.5.says: The view that Baqara 207 was revealed about Imam Ali.
shia.6.says: It is reported that many Sunni narrators considered the hadith of the city of knowledge sahih; according to the Shia it is mutawatir.
shia.7.says: The Prophet's passing, and Imam Ali's washing and burial of him.
shia.8.says: The view that the term "near kin" means the Ahl al-Bayt.
disputes.0.title: 19cueh5
Birth in the Kaaba
disputes.0.shia: That Imam Ali was born in the Kaaba is narrated in both Shia and Sunni books. Shaykh al-Mufid, in al-Irshad 1/5, and Shaykh al-Saduq, in Ilal al-Shara'i' 1/135 and al-Amali p. 195, write of this birth as his virtue.
disputes.0.sunni: That Imam Ali was born in the Kaaba is narrated in both Sunni and Shia books. Al-Hakim says in al-Mustadrak 3/483 that the reports are mutawatir. Al-Mas'udi says in Muruj al-Dhahab 2/349, "His birth was in the Kaaba." Ibn al-Mulaqqin (al-Badr al-Munir 6/489) considers this judgment of al-Hakim weak; the sentence stands in al-Mustadrak.
disputes.1.title: 1e041zr
Who is the first Muslim?
disputes.1.shia: Imam Ali believed in the Prophet at a young age and is mentioned among the first Muslims. In the Shia view, he is the first person who believed in the Prophet.
disputes.1.sunni: Imam Ali believed in the Prophet at a young age and is mentioned among the first Muslims. In the Sunni reading, they are distinguished as Khadija the first woman, Abu Bakr the first adult man, and Imam Ali the first child; there is disagreement over the order.
disputes.2.title: 1qlvqvy
About whom was Baqara 207 revealed?
disputes.2.shia: On the night of the Hijra, Imam Ali lay in the Prophet's bed; Baqara 207 is also explained through this sacrifice. In the Shia view, the verse was revealed concerning his sacrificing his life that night.
disputes.2.sunni: On the night of the Hijra, Imam Ali lay in the Prophet's bed; Baqara 207 is also explained through this sacrifice. Some of the Sunni books of tafsir and hadith transmit the same report; some also connect the verse with other persons such as Suhayb.
disputes.3.title: 1da0hhl
"La fata illa Ali, la sayfa illa Dhu al-Fiqar"
disputes.3.shia: The words "La fatâ ilâ Ali, la seifâ ilâ Zulfikâr" are remembered for the heroism of Hz. Ali. In Shiite sources, this word is common.
disputes.3.sunni: The saying "La fata illa Ali, la sayfa illa Dhu al-Fiqar" is associated with Imam Ali's heroism. Hadith scholars generally consider this saying weak or baseless; the report that Dhu al-Fiqar was a sword belonging to the Prophet is a separate matter.
disputes.4.title: 2lndh7
The authenticity of the hadith of the city of knowledge
disputes.4.shia: The saying "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate" appears in Tirmidhi, al-Jami', and al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak. In the Shia view, the saying shows Imam Ali's superiority in knowledge and has been transmitted through various chains.
disputes.4.sunni: The saying "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate" appears in Tirmidhi, al-Jami', and al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak. Its authenticity is disputed; some say sahih or hasan, others say weak or fabricated.
disputes.5.title: f95soy
Who are the "near kin" in the verse of mawadda?
disputes.5.shia: Şûrâ 23 asks for love toward the near kin; there are tafsirs that explain them as Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn. In the Shia view, these four are meant, and love for them is the recompense for the message.
disputes.5.sunni: Şûrâ 23 asks for love toward the near kin; there are tafsirs that explain them as Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn. The report of Ibn Abbas in Bukhari's Sahih, however, understands the near kin as kinship with the Quraysh.
questions.0: Ali believed in the Prophet as a child and stayed with him throughout his life. Why do you think the Prophet's upbringing made this intimacy so lasting?
questions.1: On the night of the Hijrah, a mob with swords surrounded the Prophet's house and Ali lay in his bed. Why do you think the Prophet put Ali in his bed in particular?
questions.2: The Prophet said to him, "You are my brother in this world and in the Hereafter". Why do you think the Prophet proclaimed this brotherhood for both the world and the hereafter?
questions.3: Although the city of knowledge is a city of health, the knowledge of Ali is praised. Why do you think the Prophet referred to Ali as the gateway to the city in the metaphor of knowledge?
questions.4: When Ali was washing the Prophet, there was talk in Sakife about who would take over. Why do you think Ali didn't go to that meeting and stayed with the Prophet?
summary: Imam Ali grew up beside the Prophet; he is among the first to believe, he put his life on the line on the night of the Hijra, he carried the banner in the battles, he married Lady Fatima, and he washed and buried the Prophet.
key: Imam Ali: the Prophet's brother, successor and first imam
notes.0: Imam Ali is the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, and grew up in the Prophet's house.
notes.1: He is one of the first to believe; that he believed as a child is mentioned with affection in the sources.
notes.2: On the night of the Hijra he lay in the Prophet's bed.
notes.3: In Medina the Prophet took him as a brother and married him to his daughter Lady Fatima.
notes.4: The Khaybar banner was given to Imam Ali. The saying «Gate of knowledge» is also narrated; it is not seen with the same strength in every book.

scenes.9.text: In Medina, **Ali** married **Fatimah**, the Prophet's daughter. Ali had no money to give as dowry. He sold his armor and gave the money as dowry. The house they built was modest and simple. In the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt, this marriage is said to have taken place in heaven. In this little house, **Hasan** and Husayn were born. The Prophet's lineage continued with these two grandchildren. All the imams who came after him were born from the children of this house.

scenes.10.text: Abu Zer was praying the midday prayer with the Prophet in his mosque one day. The peace of the prayer filled the inside of the mosque. The lines were closed, the voices were silenced. Just then, a beggar walked in. He stretched out his hands and asked for help from the prayers there. No one in the mosque gave him anything. The beggar waited a while, then raised his hands to the sky. He said the Prophet asked for alms in the mosque, but no one reached out to him. At that time, **Ali** was in a state of prostration. He reached out his little finger of his right hand without interrupting his prayer. She had a ring on her finger. The beggar saw the sign, approached, took the ring off his finger and walked away from the mosque. The Prophet saw Ali giving his ring as charity while he was in a state of prostration. Your protector is only God and His Messenger, and the believers who keep up prayer and pay the alms while they bow down. This verse is referred to as the guardianship verse. And their trust is in Allah and His Apostle and in the believers who give the poor-rate while they bow and prostrate themselves. Shia commentators say that the guardian in the verse was Ali, who gave his ring while in the state of prostration, after Allah and His Messenger. Many Sunni commentaries also say that this incident was narrated about Ali. Abu Zer later narrated what he saw and heard at the mosque that day.

sunni.10.says: Ibn Abbas: When Ali married Fatimah, the Prophet said to her, "Give her something". When Ali said, "I have nothing", the Prophet asked, "Where is your armor?"
sunni.11.says: He narrates from the traditions of the Sadducees and the Mujahideen that the verse was revealed to Ali and that he gave his ring as charity while he was in prostration.
sunni.12.says: The verse says that Ali descended upon giving his ring to the poor during the recitation of prayer.
sunni.13.says: He writes that the verse descended on Ali, that the beggar asked Ali for help in a state of prostration, and that Ali gave him the ring on his little finger.
sunni.14.says: Abu Zer narrates extensively that no one gave to the beggar who came to the mosque at noon prayer, that he pointed to the ring on the little finger of Ali's right hand in prostration and that the beggar took the ring; then he writes that the verse came down.
sunni.15.says: He narrates from Abu Zer that a beggar asked for help in the mosque while praying with the Prophet, but no one gave it, that Ali, in his bow, reached out his ring finger and the beggar took the ring, and then wrote that the verse came down.
sunni.16.says: He narrates that Ali gave his ring when he was in prostration. Ibn Abbas also mentions the trials of the Suddis and the Mujahideen. He then says that none of these accounts are true because of the weakness of their evidence and the mechality of their prophets. He reads the verse as a province of all believers.
shia.9.says: He writes that the verse descended on Ali and narrates that the ring was given as charity when he was in prostration with Abu Zer Tarikh.
disputes.6.title: kdyi2g
Who did the Maide 55 come down on?
disputes.6.shia: In the Shia, Ma'idah 55, descends upon Ali's giving his ring as charity while he was in prostration and announces his guardianship. Tabersy, in the Mecmau'l-Beyân, conveys the cause of this downfall.
disputes.6.sunni: Tabari, Waheed, Zemahshari, Razi and Sa'lebi, the verse conveys its connection with the giving of the ring by Ali while he was in prostration. Ibn Kathir, however, considers the evidence of these reports weak, and reads the verse as the province of all believers.
